item.title: Dallas sports anchor lands new TV gig after hometown stint
item.description: Sports anchor and reporter Abbi Bennett is joined CBS Austin after nearly a year at NBC 5 in Dallas-Fort Worth. (FOX 21) A Dallas-Fort Worth sports anchor is heading to Austin after spending nearly a year reporting for a TV station she grew up watching. Abbi Bennett, who freelanced as a sports anchor and reporter for NBC 5 in Dallas-Fort Worth from November 2025 through September 2026, announced Sunday that she's joining CBS Austin in the same role. "Dallas, you've been so good to me this last year!" Bennett wrote on Instagram. Bennett expressed gratitude for the opportunity to work in her hometown, describing her departure as bittersweet. "This chapter has brought some incredible people, opportunities, and memories, making it a tough one to close," she wrote. "But as one door closes, another one opens and I'm excited for what's ahead!" View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abbi Bennett (@abbi.bennett) Her arrival comes nearly a month after former CBS Austin sports anchor and reporter Darby Brown left the station for a new role at 12News in Phoenix, Ariz., her hometown. Brown was among those congratulating Bennett on her announcement, commenting, "Yay!!! Congrats you are gonna crush it!" Before returning to Texas, Bennett spent three years as a sports anchor and reporter at FOX21 News in Colorado Springs, Colo. , where she anchored evening sports broadcasts. During her first two years at the station, she earned back-to-back Best Sportscaster awards from the Colorado Broadcasters Association in 2023 and 2024. Bennett graduated from the University of Oklahoma in 2022 with a degree in broadcast journalism and a minor in sports management. During college, she participated in several student-produced broadcasts, including OU Nightly , Sooner Sports Pad and Gameday U . She also served as vice president and president of the Association for Women in Sports Media. Despite both her parents attending the University of Texas , Bennett chose Oklahoma after visiting the campus. Growing up, she developed her love of sports watching the Cowboys, Mavericks and Rangers with her father. She also played soccer, which became her favorite sport. item.title: Ravens make two kinds of brutal NFL history with horrible second-half problems
item.description: Ravens make two kinds of brutal NFL history with horrible second-half problems originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens are 4-3 in the regular season, which isn't bad considering they've been without Lamar Jackson for a couple of weeks now. But the team's Week 7 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals was a brutal one that deserves some flak. The final score of 35-13 is bad enough, but the context of that score is made so much worse: they had a 13-0 lead at halftime. ESPN's Ben Baby and The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia shared two brutal NFL history-making statistics from this loss that highlight just how terrible this team has been in the second half of games this season. Ravens have a major second-half problem amid two brutal feats of NFL history "The Ravens rank 1st in the NFL with a +65 point differential in the first half. The Ravens rank 32nd in the NFL with a -70 point differential in the second half," Kapadia shared. Those statistics from the 2026 NFL season show just how bad this Ravens team has been in the second half of games this year. While they get out to strong starts, they've been thoroughly outscored in the second half of games this season. The worst such game just happened, with the Ravens' blown 13-point lead to the Bengals being an all-time terrible one. As Baby notes, "Per ESPN Research, the Ravens are the 3rd team in NFL history to lose a game by 20+ points after leading by 13+ points at halftime. Other two times it happened: 1950 and 1941." MORE : NFL insider reveals Browns might not be done with Deshaun Watson after 2026 What Ravens fans just witnessed in Week 7 with the team's massive loss to the Bengals was something that the NFL hasn't seen in roughly 75 years. Tyler Huntley and this Ravens offense hit a blockade in this game and didn't come even remotely close to making this a competitive game before it was over, despite holding a 13-point lead at halftime. This isn't just a one-off issue either, as Kapadia's statistics show this has been a problem all year for the Ravens. They continue to thrive in first halves but collapse in the second half. If the Ravens want any chance of contending this year, this problem has to be fixed, and soon. Jackson's return could help, but facing the Buffalo Bills in Week 8, the Ravens might be in serious trouble with this major second-half problem. item.description: (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) (Photo by FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Ballon d’Or signifies the best footballer of the year, taking into account individual performance, team achievements, class, and fair play. French sports magazine France Football started the award in 1956, and it has since become the most prestigious individual award in world football. Since its inception, the Golden Ball has hopped across several nations, following bona fide talent and achievements. However, factors such as luck, longevity, perception management, and PR skills play significant roles in the final result. Despite this complex mix of variables in a sport as dynamic as football, some nations have managed to secure multiple wins. Although these countries have accumulated several awards, they vary by their distribution patterns. France, Germany, Brazil, and Italy have multiple players who got their hands on the Golden Ball across different positions on the pitch. On the other hand, Argentina, Portugal, and the Netherlands have been propped up on the shoulders of individual serial winners. Let us take a look at the nations with the most wins and the players who won the award for them. 8 wins – France and Argentina Two nations possess a rich footballing heritage, but their dominance of the Ballon d’Or manifests in totally different ways. France is renowned for producing electric attacking talent. Raymond Kopa won France’s first Ballon d’Or in 1958. The versatile attacker played for Stade de Reims and Real Madrid. Kopa was followed by a series of attackers and attacking midfielders who won the prestigious award for France. The legendary Michel Platini won it three times in a row from 1983 to 1985. Widely regarded as one of the best goal-scoring attacking midfielders, Platini’s instinct for goal, dead-ball ability, and vision to set up teammates were unmatched in his era. Jean-Pierre Papin and Zinedine Zidane added two more to the tally, with Zizou’s Ballon d’Or coming on the back of the 1998 French World Cup victory. The latest winners, Karim Benzema and Ousmane Dembele, brought home the Ballon d’Or after victorious domestic and Europ ean campaigns in 2022 and 2025. Argentina, on the other hand, has one winner who bagged the Ballon d’Or all eight times for his nation. Lionel Messi, one of the greatest players in the sport, has been a serial winner of the award. Bursting onto the scene for Barcelona in 2006, Messi quickly rose through the ranks to rule the sport. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Tears Up After Jalen Williams Is Stretchered Off Court with Horrific Leg Injury
item.description: Jalen Williams Credit: Zach Beeker/NBAE via Getty NEED TO KNOW Jalen Williams suffered a gruesome ankle injury during Sunday’s game The Oklahoma City Thunder star fell onto his lower left leg after going up for a layup in the waning minutes of the game Teammate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander teared up talking about the loss of Williams after the game As his Oklahoma City Thunder teammates looked on in seeming disbelief and shock, Jalen Williams suffered a gruesome injury on Sunday, Oct. 25 in a game against the Los Angeles Clippers. Williams, 25, fell on his left ankle while driving to the basket late in the game and immediately collapsed to the floor. In the immediate moments afterward, Paycom Center went silent as players including reigning NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander draped their faces in towels as if to un-see the injury, which resulted in Williams being taken off the floor on a stretcher. No immediate update has been provided on Williams’ injury as of Monday morning. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! The former Santa Clara standout’s injury comes three games into the season and after a year in which he missed 49 games due to a variety of injuries including a hamstring strain and recovery from wrist surgery. In an interview with the team’s sideline reporter Nick Gallo after the Thunder won, 108-101 — and as Thunder players kept a respectful but unusual distance behind him in support — Gilgeous-Alexander had trouble keeping his composure. Jalen Williams Credit: Joshua Gateley/Getty “Just feel bad for him,” the Thunder All-Star guard, 28, said, fighting back tears. “Nothing more than that.” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault summed up the team’s collective emotions in the post-game presser. “We’re not doing great,” Daigneault, 41, said. For Williams, who played a key role on the 2025 NBA championship team and has averaged 17.9 points per game over his first 251 career starts, the timing of the injury is heartbreaking — and it’s also such for the Oklahoma community, where he’s a beloved player. “Our whole city will have JDub in our thoughts and prayers as he deals with this adversity and as he makes his way through his recovery,” Oklahoma City Mayor David Holt posted on social media after the game. item.title: Tyrese Maxey gets honest about the 76ers' biggest problem from the team's first loss
item.description: Tyrese Maxey gets honest about the 76ers' biggest problem from the team's first loss originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers suffered their first loss of the 2026-27 NBA season on Sunday against the Detroit Pistons . It was a tough 106-93 loss, especially because they were struggling with their rebounding. Detroit resoundingly won the rebounding battle, 54 to the 76ers ' 37. Of course, this was mostly because the 76ers did not have their big men. Joel Embiid had to sit out the game due to plantar fasciitis injury management, and LeBron James started at center. Tyrese Maxey gets real about the 76ers' biggest problem in the 2026-27 season The 76ers tried their best, but their center problems might be a long-term issue for this season. Head coach Nick Nurse elected to start LeBron James against the Pistons , while keeping Adem Bona in his off-the-bench role. They were quite short-handed because they did not have Embiid or Jabari Walker, while also having a long-term injury to supposed back-up center Ariel Hukporti. This eventually became the issue that led to them losing against the Pistons. MORE: LeBron James' honest reaction about starting at center for the 76ers Detroit did not have Jalen Duren due to a hamstring injury, but the Pistons replaced his rebounding through a team-wide effort. John Collins led the team with 11 rebounds, but Ron Holland II, Paul Reed, Cade Cunningham, and Daniss Jenkins all chipped in with at least eight rebounds. This led to Maxey speaking after the game about having these rebounding troubles. He made fun of the situation, but there is still a lot of truth to what he was saying. "If some of our tall guys could come back, that would be great. We gotta hit, box out, try to fight, man, gotta figure it out. When the ball come off the rim, gotta do whatever we got to do to get that rebound," Maxey said after the loss to Detroit . Moving forward, both the coaches and the front office must find a way to address this issue. James should not be playing center for extended periods even if he is willing to play that role. He could get injured through that, so finding the right balance with the centers is a priority. item.title: Lazio Fans to Take Over at Mapei at 10,000 Flock to Sassuolo
item.description: Lazio Fans to Take Over at Mapei at 10,000 Flock to Sassuolo The travelling Lazio supporters could outnumber their hosts on Tuesday, as 10,000 join the team on the trip to Sassuolo. Lazio Fans Refusing to Attend Home Games The club’s organised fan groups have been refusing to attend home games at the Stadio Olimpico since January, as part of their ongoing protest against unpopular Lazio president Claudio Lotito . The aim is to deprive the administration of matchday revenue and pile more pressure on the patron, who is being urged to sell the club. Player Ratings: Lazio 2-1 Parma – Belahyane & Taylor Run The Show Last week, Lazio sporting director Angelo Fabiani urged the fans to reconsider their decision , especially with the team registering sensational results since the start of the Serie A campaign, winning seven and drawing one in their first eight league contests. However, the supporters’ groups swiftly rejected the invitation, insisting that their rift with Lotito goes well beyond sporting results. Lazio Able to Count on Large Support on the Road While a small section of the fanbase has been attending Lazio’s home games, large numbers have been accompanying Gennaro Gattuso’s men in their travels, as witnessed in Bologna, Udine, Venice, and most recently Turin (against Juventus). Travelling Lazio Supporters Will Invade Sassuolo According to Il Corriere dello Sport (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), the midweek schedule will do little to deter the loyal club supporters, as 10,000 strong will make the trip to Sassuolo to support the Biancocelesti on Tuesday. A Déjà Vu at the Mapei? The Mapei Stadium’s current capacity is circa 21,000, with only 4,000 seats allocated to away supporters. However, we’ve seen travelling supporters invade this particular ground in the past, most famously AC Milan fans who took over the stands to watch Stefano Pioli’s men clinch the Scudetto title on the final day of the 2021/22 season.

On Saturday, it also served as the capital of the college football universe. ESPN’s College GameDay rolled into town ahead of the marquee Big 12 showdown, adding greater anticipation to the 100th consecutive sellout at Rice-Eccles Stadium. A crowd of 51,864 fans mostly dressed in black, adhering to Utah’s annual “Dark Mode” theme, arrived to hoping to witness their Utes revel in the spotlight. The program had largely flown under the radar in the past two seasons despite owning the country’s longest win streak. That streak extended Saturday night in Salt Lake City as No. 10 Utah rallied from a second half double-digit deficit to upend No. 14 Houston, 21-13. It marked the 13th consecutive win as the Utes remained undefeated under first-year head coach Morgan Scalley. “A reminder, it’s hard to win in college football,” Scalley said. “So grateful for our guys, their fight. That’s what you need. I don’t really care about the stats. I’m so proud of these guys, just their fight.” The Utes averaged over 40 points per game prior to their toughest matchup to date. However, Kevin McGiven’s electrifying offense sputtered early against the Cougars. For the first time since he took over as offensive coordinator, Utah failed to score an opening drive touchdown. The slow start continued, and the Utes were shut out at halftime for the first time since Oct. 19, 2024. “I’ve seen locker rooms where there’s a panic and people start freaking out at each other, but it was awesome,” Scalley said of the halftime demeanor. “It was a really good example of talking things through and seeing things for what they are.” Even while Utah’s offense struggled to find the end zone, quarterback Devon Dampier kept the Utes moving with his legs. He rushed for 80 yards in the first half, regularly evading Houston defenders and extending plays. It was only a matter of time before his mobility changed the game. item.description: Motorsport photo This October's NASCAR Cup Series race at Talladega Superspeedway was certainly a memorable one, and pretty much all title contenders encountered issues except for the one already sitting atop the standings. item.title: Has Thierry Henry ever won the Ballon d'Or? Arsenal and Barcelona legend's history in top award
item.description: Has Thierry Henry ever won the Ballon d'Or? Arsenal and Barcelona legend's history in top award originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Considered one of the greatest strikers of the modern age, Thierry Henry is revered within the history of football over the last few decades. As a leading member of the Arsenal Invincibles team that went unbeaten across an entire Premier League season, Henry has won nearly every title there is in the sport — from three different major European league titles to a UEFA Champions League, and even a World Cup. So, he has obviously also been just as accomplished on the individual level as well, surely? It would track that Henry has won the Ballon d'Or previously, as the world's most coveted individual prize in football. Oddly, the truth may surprise you as the Ballon d'Or can sometimes prove more elusive than we think even for the all-time greats of the game. MORE: Who has won the most Ballon d'Or trophies? Did Thierry Henry ever win the Ballon d'Or? Despite being nominated nine times for the Ballon d'Or, no, Thierry Henry did not ever win the coveted individual award. The famed striker came exceedingly close on two occasions, but lost out twice to non-goal scorers on both occasions. Henry came closest in 2003, when he was with Arsenal, finishing second to Juventus midfielder Pavel Nedved, who had led the Italian side to not only a Serie A title but also the brink of the Champions League title, falling to fellow Italian giants AC Milan in the final on a penalty shootout. Three years later, in 2006, Henry would finish third, behind defender Fabio Cannavaro and goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon. Unfortunately for Henry, the years he put up his greatest individual numbers did not coincide with the years he secured his most impressive team accomplishments. While at Arsenal, Henry was great within the context of the English domestic league, but they only reached past the Champions League quarterfinals once during his time with the club, coming in 2005/06 when they were runners-up, but that year he finished behind two Italians that lifted the World Cup title. After moving to Barcelona , Henry would perform better in the Champions League, which matters most to Ballon d'Or voters, but he was less of an individual juggernaut by then. The year he won his Champions League title, the 2008/09 campaign, teammate Lionel Messi would be the Ballon d'Or winner. It just never came together for Henry. Thierry Henry awards, titles Thierry Henry won an incredible amount of silverware during his time as a player, but received surprisingly few individual honors for a player so highly revered in the history of the game. item.title: Cam Skattebo injury update offers good news for Giants RB
item.description: The New York Giants exited the Week 7 game against the Houston Texans with an injury concern for running back Cam Skattebo . During his 42-yard run that set up the Giants’ winning touchdown in overtime, Skattebo pulled up with a leg injury that he later confirmed after the game was a hamstring issue. We didn’t know the severity of the injury at the time, though, so Skattebo wasn’t out of the woods quite yet. However, on Monday morning, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Skattebo’s injury is not considered serious and he should be fine. MORE: Cam Skattebo calls out NFL hypocrisy over rare helmet penalty “All indications this morning are (Skattebo) should be OK, especially with the team on a bye this weekend. A rare, welcome instance for NYG to not have an IR candidate after a game,” Garafolo reported. The Giants’ bye comes at a perfect time, as Skattebo will now have two weeks to get right before Big Blue returns to action in Week 9 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Taking back RB1 duties New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) runs with the ball during overtime against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Skattebo bounced back in a big way for the Giants in Week 7, with the second-year back finishing with a career-high 124 yards while also scoring a touchdown. The aforementioned 42-yard scamper was the longest of his career. It was a much-needed performance after Skattebo got himself benched the week prior because of fumbling issues. Skattebo led the way for the Giants with his 17 carries, but Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy mixed in with five and six carries, respectively. MORE: 5 teams with shocking records heading into Week 8 Like Skattebo, Tracy got hurt during the game and had to exit early, which set Singletary up to score the game-winning touchdown on a 30-yard run. “It was awesome to be able to show Coach and show the team that we have running backs in the backfield that can do it,” Skattebo said, per ESPN’s Jordan Raanan . “Pretty cool.” The Giants have been speculated about as a team that could potentially make a trade for a running back at the trade deadline given their woes at the position this season. item.title: Arturo Vidal thinking about returning to Juventus
item.description: Arturo Vidal thinking about returning to Juventus Arturo Vidal is one of the best midfielders Juventus has had, and he enjoyed a very fruitful spell on their team between 2011 and 2015. He would go on to play for teams like Bayern Munich and Barcelona, but it was at Juve that he enjoyed a lot of success, and he played the most league games of his career for them in Europe. He continues to play at 39 and is now playing as a centre-back, but the former midfielder is still thinking about Juve, and he expects to be back at the club as a coach. Most players who spend a long time on the books of Juve never forget the club and continue to see it as one of the best places they have played. Vidal’s Love for Juventus Vidal is one of them, and he hints that he would go into coaching when he stops playing and will be back coaching at Juve. He said via Calciomercato : “Juventus is the club I remain closest to. I feel a special affection for the fans and my teammates; we won so much. Those were wonderful years; Italy will always be in my heart: my children grew up there. “Llorente said that Juventus needs a Vidal to get back to winning ways? His words make me proud. I will return to Juventus in the future, as a coach. But now I still want to play, and by changing positions I have extended my career: I feel comfortable in defense and recently they ranked me among the best central defenders in South America.” (Photo by Christian Alvarenga/Getty Images) A Future in Coaching Vidal’s words show the deep bond he has with Juventus, and his desire to return as a coach is a sign of his affection for the club. The Chilean’s legacy in Turin is secure, and the fans will welcome him back. The midfielder’s career has been remarkable, and his ability to adapt to a new position at 39 is a testament to his professionalism. His future in coaching seems certain, and Juventus could be his destination. The coming years will show whether Vidal returns to Juve, but his love for the club is clear. The fans will be hoping he does, and his experience would be invaluable. The bond between player and club endures.

item.title: Glazer family wait for right chance to sell Manchester United amid Sir Jim Ratcliffe concerns
item.description: Glazer family wait for right chance to sell Manchester United amid Sir Jim Ratcliffe concerns Manchester United’s majority-owning Glazer family are reportedly waiting for the right opportunity to sell the club, while allowing minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to continue overseeing football operations despite the deepening crisis at Old Trafford. Ratcliffe’s investment has not delivered the promised revival The Glazers announced a strategic review in November 2022 which considered outside investment, a full sale or another transaction involving United. Ratcliffe completed his investment on 20 February 2024, paying approximately £1.25 billion for a 27.7% stake and receiving control of football operations. United subsequently cut around 250 jobs in 2024 before announcing plans in February 2025 to remove up to another 200 positions. On the pitch, manager Ruben Amorim was dismissed in January 2026 after 14 months, with head coach Michael Carrick initially returning on a caretaker basis before receiving a contract until 2028 in May. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth extended a miserable run and left United 16th in the Premier League, two points above the bottom of the table. Carrick’s team have won only one of their opening eight league matches, with the Bournemouth performance exposing further problems with their pressing, passing and defending . Sale conditions and concerns over Ratcliffe The Glazers retain nearly 72% of United and control any future sale. The agreement with Ratcliffe also contains a drag-along provision which allows them to require him to sell his stake as part of a takeover by a third party ( via ESPN ). Ratcliffe is entitled to receive at least $33 per share if a sale takes place before February 2027. That protection then expires, while United’s shares closed at $20.61 on the New York Stock Exchange last Friday. “One source has told ESPN that the Glazers are waiting for the right time to cash in and sell,” reporter Mark Ogden claims. So might it be that the Glazers are waiting until that February deadline before finally selling the club? Before United fans get too hopeful, ESPN notes that: “There is no market right now for investors looking to buy a Premier League team, especially one with United’s problems. Uncertainty over the outcome of Manchester City’s appeal against a guilty verdict on 114 of 115 Premier League charges means that any potential buyer is likely to wait for that process to play out. item.title: Cliff Diver Molly Carlson Makes History as First Woman to Dive Off Iceberg
item.description: Molly Carlson makes history after diving from iceberg Credit: Mason Mashon / Red Bull Content Pool via AP NEED TO KNOW Canadian cliff diver Molly Carlson became the first woman to dive from a free-standing iceberg Carlson and Red Bull released a documentary showing her learning to climb ice and complete the historic dive She described the dive as “definitely the scariest thing I’ve ever done” Cliff diver Molly Carlson made history with Red Bull. The 28-year-old professional cliff diver became the first woman to dive from a free-standing iceberg, jumping 50 feet above water off the Newfoundland coast in Canada. In a documentary shared on YouTube by Carlson and Red Bull, the Ontario-born athlete shared her experience training for months before the historic 50-foot dive. “They can split, collapse or roll without warning,” she tells viewers. In one scene, Carlson tells her partner, fellow professional high-diver Aidan Heslop, that the stunt is “so much more dangerous than we thought.” Molly Carlson makes history jumping from an iceberg Credit: Mason Mashon / Red Bull Content Pool via AP Under the guidance of longtime ice climber Will Gadd, Carlson performed her highest backwards dive yet. Before that, however, she had to learn how to climb the ice. Gadd mentored her through the experience, and in an interview, she described him as “almost my dad in this story,” per Red Bull . “He’s the one keeping me safe,” she said. “He’s the one teaching me. He’s the one making sure I understand what we’re getting into.” The athlete and influencer — who has fostered a loyal online community called the Brave Gang , in which she encourages her millions of followers to practice bravery and self-love — admitted that jumping from icebergs, and even climbing them, is “incredibly dangerous” and described the dive as “definitely the scariest thing I’ve ever done.” “I felt like I was in the air for like 10 minutes,” she said. Carlson, who has publicly shared she deals with anxiety, told Red Bull her historic feat felt like “therapy on the ice wall” and “represented so much more than diving.” She added, “You only see 10 percent of the iceberg on the surface. People can be struggling under the surface, and people can have so much more going on than what they show. I felt like this project represented that perfectly.” “I’m doing this for all the people that might be scared to show what’s under the surface,” Carlson said. Take PEOPLE with you! item.description: José Mourinho led Real Madrid to a 2-1 win against Barcelona on Sunday -Credit:Alex Caparros, Getty Images This is precisely why Real Madrid brought José Mourinho back. Florentino Pérez's choice to appoint Mourinho in the summer, following a dismal spell under Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa, drew widespread criticism for appearing rooted in nostalgia. Mourinho had last been at the helm of Real some 13 years prior, and his managerial methods have faced considerable scrutiny in recent times. Yet his knee slide celebration after Kylian Mbappé's second goal secured a crucial 2-1 victory over Barcelona on Sunday night was precisely the kind of moment Pérez must have had in mind when making that call. Erik ten Hag 'embarrassed' by Scott McTominay transfer as ex-Man United manager slams club bosses Bruno Fernandes suggests he no longer cares about Manchester United after Carrick call -Credit:David Ramos, Getty Images It was quintessential Mourinho. Real entered the contest as underdogs against a flying Barça side and controlled just 37 percent of possession. But they made their opportunities count. Mbappé's opener owed a considerable debt to fortune, with Gerard Martin's attempted clearance deflecting off his shin and into the net. Barça drew level through Raphinha before Eduardo Camavinga drove into the penalty area and teed up Mbappé to tap home the match-winning goal in the 87th minute. The 63-year-old Mourinho unleashed his trademark knee slide along the touchline and, following a courteous handshake with Barça head coach Hansi Flick, delivered the kind of cutting remark he's long been celebrated for. "I dedicate this win to the Barça fans who came to the hotel and kept singing all day, I couldn't take my nap," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV, via The Mirror . "I didn't nap, but I did beat their team. A big hug to them." Mourinho has claimed six victories and suffered six defeats in El Clásico during two spells as Real boss, yet he remains unbeaten in the last six encounters, recording four wins and two draws. He thrives on the grandest stages, and Real now trail their rivals by just three points, sitting one behind Atlético Madrid in La Liga.
